set_title: Diabetes names: sweet urine (mellitus) vs tasteless urine (insipidus) and their look-alikes
stem: A 35-year-old man with schizophrenia drinks about 10 L of water daily. He feels well apart from mild confusion. Serum sodium is 128 mEq/L and urine osmolality is 80 mOsm/kg. After 12 hours without water, his urine osmolality rises to 600 mOsm/kg.
oneliner: 35M with schizophrenia + 10 L water daily, Na 128, dilute urine + concentrates when water is withheld → ?

whyNot.A: Central form raises sodium and fails to concentrate; his **sodium is 128, urine concentrates**
whyNot.C: Type 2 diabetes makes glucose-laden urine; his is **dilute with low sodium**
whyNot.D: SIADH has concentrated urine at baseline; his is **dilute from drinking 10 L**
whyNot.E: Nephrogenic form cannot concentrate; his urine **rises to 600 with water restriction**

why: Drinking too much: excess water dilutes the blood and the kidney appropriately makes dilute urine. **Low sodium that concentrates with water restriction** is primary polydipsia.

idea.rule: Low sodium + dilute urine + concentrates when water withheld = polydipsia.

set_title: Schizo- names: schizophrenia vs schizophreniform vs schizoaffective vs schizoid vs schizotypal
stem: A 24-year-old man has heard voices commenting on his actions for 3 months. He believes his neighbors are monitoring him. His speech is disorganized and he has stopped attending classes. He has no episodes of low or elevated mood. Drug screening and brain MRI are normal. He functioned well before this.
oneliner: 24M + voices and paranoia for 3 months, disorganized speech + no mood episode + normal drug screen → ?

whyNot.A: Schizophrenia needs symptoms over 6 months; his illness is **3 months**
whyNot.C: Brief psychotic disorder lasts under 1 month; his has lasted **3 months**
whyNot.D: Schizotypal has odd beliefs without true psychosis; he has **hallucinations and delusions**
whyNot.E: Schizoaffective needs mood episodes; he has **no mood episode**

why: Schizophrenia-like, shorter: same symptoms but duration of 1 to 6 months. **Psychosis for 3 months without a mood episode** is schizophreniform disorder.

idea.rule: Schizophrenia symptoms lasting 1 to 6 months = schizophreniform.

set_title: Schizo- names: schizophrenia vs schizophreniform vs schizoaffective vs schizoid vs schizotypal
stem: A 30-year-old woman has had a manic episode with pressured speech and grandiose delusions lasting 3 months. During it she also heard voices telling her what to do. After her mania resolved, the voices and a belief that her phone is bugged continued for 3 more weeks. She has been treated twice before with similar episodes.
oneliner: 30F + 3 months of mania with voices and delusions + psychosis persists 3 weeks after mood resolves → ?

whyNot.B: Schizophreniform has no mood episode; she had **full mania with psychosis**
whyNot.C: Schizotypal has eccentric beliefs without hallucinations; she has **mania and persistent voices**
whyNot.D: Schizoid personality has detachment without psychosis; she has **voices and delusions**
whyNot.E: Brief psychotic disorder lasts under 1 month; hers has **recurred over months with mania**

why: Schizophrenia plus mood episodes. **Psychosis continuing for 2 or more weeks after the mood episode resolves** is schizoaffective disorder.

idea.rule: Mood episode plus psychosis lasting 2+ weeks without mood symptoms = schizoaffective.

set_title: Schizo- names: schizophrenia vs schizophreniform vs schizoaffective vs schizoid vs schizotypal
stem: A 40-year-old man lives alone and works nights stocking shelves. He has no friends, never dated, and says he does not miss company. He prefers to spend weekends reading about astronomy. He shows little emotion when praised or criticized. He has no hallucinations, delusions or odd beliefs. He came in only for a dental infection.
oneliner: 40M + lives alone, no friends, no wish for company + flat affect + no hallucinations or odd beliefs → ?

whyNot.A: Schizotypal has magical thinking and odd speech; he has **no odd beliefs**
whyNot.B: Schizophrenia has hallucinations or delusions; he has **none and works steadily**
whyNot.C: Schizophreniform needs psychosis; he has **no hallucinations or delusions**
whyNot.E: Schizoaffective needs psychosis and mood episodes; he has **neither**

why: Schizophrenia-like detachment without psychosis. **A solitary person with no wish for relationships, flat affect and no odd beliefs** is schizoid.

idea.rule: Loner who is content alone, no odd beliefs = schizoid.
also: Differs from avoidant, who wants friends

set_title: Schizo- names: schizophrenia vs schizophreniform vs schizoaffective vs schizoid vs schizotypal
stem: A 35-year-old woman is referred by her employer because coworkers find her odd. She wears several layers of mismatched clothing and says she senses when her sister is in danger because of telepathy. Her speech is vague and over-elaborate. She has few friends and is anxious in groups. She denies hallucinations and her thinking is not delusional.
oneliner: 35F + odd dress, belief in telepathy, vague speech + social anxiety + no true hallucinations or delusions → ?

whyNot.A: Schizoid has no odd beliefs; she has **magical thinking and odd dress**
whyNot.C: Schizophrenia has fixed delusions and hallucinations; she has **none**
whyNot.D: Schizoaffective needs psychosis plus mood episodes; she has **neither**
whyNot.E: Delusional disorder needs a fixed false belief; her thinking is **not delusional**

why: Odd schizophrenia-type personality without full psychosis. **Magical thinking, eccentric dress and vague speech** is schizotypal personality disorder.

idea.rule: Eccentric, magical thinking, no true psychosis = schizotypal.

set_title: Trich- names: Trichomonas, Trichinella, Trichuris, Trichophyton, trichotillomania
stem: A 14-year-old girl has patchy hair loss on her scalp. The patches contain broken hairs of different lengths with no scale or inflammation. She admits pulling her hair when anxious and has tried to stop.
oneliner: 14-year-old girl, patchy scalp hair loss + broken hairs of varied lengths + no scale + pulls hair when anxious → ?

whyNot.A: Trichomonas vaginalis is a genital infection; she has **patchy hair loss**
whyNot.B: Trichinella is a muscle roundworm; she has **broken hairs of varied lengths**
whyNot.D: Trichuris is a colonic worm; she has **scalp hair loss**
whyNot.E: Trichophyton causes scaly patches with hyphae; hers are **non-scaly with hairs of varied length**

why: Trich (hair) + tillo (pull) + mania: a compulsion to pull out hair. **Patchy loss with broken hairs of varied length and no scale** in an anxious teen.

idea.rule: Trichotillomania: broken hairs of different lengths; tinea capitis: scale and hyphae.

set_title: Antipsychotic movement names: acute dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia
stem: A 22-year-old man with schizophrenia received his first dose of haloperidol yesterday. Today his neck is twisted to the right, his jaw is clenched and his eyes are rolled upward. He is frightened but alert. Temperature is 37 C and muscle enzymes are normal.
oneliner: 22M, first haloperidol dose yesterday + neck twisted, jaw clenched, eyes rolled up, alert → ?

whyNot.A: Akathisia is inner restlessness; he has **fixed twisted neck and upward gaze**
whyNot.C: Tardive dyskinesia appears after months; his spasm began **after the first dose**
whyNot.D: Drug-induced parkinsonism takes weeks and gives rigidity; his spasm began **within a day**
whyNot.E: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome has fever and high CK; his **temperature and enzymes are normal**

why: Dys = abnormal, tonia = tone. Sudden sustained muscle contraction: **neck twist and upward gaze within a day of haloperidol**.

idea.rule: Acute dystonia = hours; akathisia = days; parkinsonism = weeks; TD = years.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Hours to days: neck twist, oculogyric crisis**
**Months to years: lip smacking, tongue movements**

set_title: Antipsychotic movement names: acute dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia
stem: A 30-year-old woman started haloperidol 2 weeks ago. She now cannot sit through a meal, shifts her legs constantly and paces the hall. She says she feels she must move and is anxious. Tone, gait and reflexes are normal, and she has no tremor.
oneliner: 30F, 2 weeks on haloperidol + cannot sit still, constant leg shifting and pacing, normal tone → ?

whyNot.A: Drug-induced parkinsonism causes rigidity and tremor; her **tone is normal, no tremor**
whyNot.B: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome has fever and rigidity; she has **normal tone and no fever**
whyNot.C: Acute dystonia is sustained spasm of muscles; she has **pacing and inner restlessness**
whyNot.D: Tardive dyskinesia has lip smacking after years; she has **been on treatment 2 weeks**

why: A = not, kathis = sitting. Inability to sit still: **inner restlessness and pacing within weeks of an antipsychotic**.

idea.rule: Akathisia = can't sit; treat with propranolol or lower the dose.

set_title: Antipsychotic movement names: acute dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia
stem: A 60-year-old man has taken haloperidol for schizophrenia for 12 years. He now has repetitive lip smacking, tongue protrusion and chewing movements that he does not control. They disappear during sleep. Tone is normal and he has no rigidity.
oneliner: 60M, haloperidol 12 years + involuntary lip smacking, tongue movements, absent in sleep → ?

whyNot.A: Akathisia is restlessness with pacing; he has **repetitive orofacial movements**
whyNot.B: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome has fever and rigidity; he has **normal tone and no fever**
whyNot.C: Acute dystonia is sustained spasm in days; his movements arose **after 12 years**
whyNot.D: Drug-induced parkinsonism has rigidity and bradykinesia; his tone is **normal**

why: Tardive = late. Dopamine receptors become supersensitive: **lip smacking and tongue movements after years of antipsychotics**.

idea.rule: Tardive dyskinesia = late, orofacial; treat with valbenazine.
also: Switch to clozapine or add VMAT2 inhibitor
